title: Which token should I use for muted text?
summary: Use --color-text-muted (#64748b) for muted text on white, and switch to --color-text-secondary on indigo tinted surfaces.
short: Use `var(--color-text-muted)` for muted text. It is #64748b (slate 500), which measures 4.76:1 on white and is the lightest color allowed for text on white. On `--color-primary-surface` (#eef2ff) it fails AA at 4.26:1, so use `var(--color-text-secondary)` there. Do not use `--color-text-disabled` or slate 400 for readable text.

sections.heading: The answer: --color-text-muted
body: The muted text role is `--color-text-muted`, with the value #64748b (slate 500). On the white surface `--color-surface` (#ffffff) it measures 4.76:1, which passes WCAG 2.2 AA for normal text (4.5:1 minimum).
Slate 500 is the floor for muted text on white. Never use a color lighter than #64748b for text. Slate 400 (#94a3b8) measures 2.56:1 on white and fails, so it is not allowed for text.

Muted text has two known limits. On `--color-surface-secondary` (#f8fafc) it measures 4.55:1, which passes but leaves a thin margin. On `--color-primary-surface` (#eef2ff) it measures 4.26:1, which fails AA for normal text. On an indigo tint, use `--color-text-secondary` instead.

sections.heading: The six text role tokens
body: All six text roles are neutral slate. Choose by the job the text does, not by how it looks. Ratios are measured on white (#ffffff).

sections.heading: Recommended and avoided usage
body: ✓ Recommended: Use `--color-text-muted` for secondary metadata on white surfaces.
Rule: Muted text uses `--color-text-muted` (#64748b) on white, and nothing lighter than slate 500 is used for text.
Why: #64748b measures 4.76:1 on white, which passes WCAG 2.2 AA for normal text. Lighter slate values fall below the 4.5:1 minimum.
✕ Avoid: Using `--color-text-disabled` or slate 400 for muted text.
Rule: Do not use `--color-text-disabled` (#cbd5e1) or slate 400 (#94a3b8) for readable text.
Why: `--color-text-disabled` measures 1.48:1 on white and is reserved for disabled states. Slate 400 measures 2.56:1 on white and fails AA. Readers cannot reliably see either one.

faq.q: Which token should I use for muted text on a white background?
faq.a: Use var(--color-text-muted), which is #64748b (slate 500). It measures 4.76:1 on white and passes WCAG 2.2 AA for normal text.

faq.q: Can I use a lighter gray for muted text?
faq.a: No. #64748b is the floor for muted text on white. Slate 400 (#94a3b8) measures 2.56:1 on white and fails, so it is not allowed for text.

faq.q: What should I use for muted text on an indigo tinted background?
faq.a: Use var(--color-text-secondary), which is #475569. Muted text on --color-primary-surface (#eef2ff) measures 4.26:1 and fails AA for normal text, while secondary text measures 7.58:1 on white.

faq.q: Is --color-text-disabled a good choice for less important text?
faq.a: No. --color-text-disabled (#cbd5e1) measures 1.48:1 on white and is for disabled control states only. It is never used for readable text.

faq.q: Does muted text pass contrast on the light gray surface?
faq.a: It passes, with a thin margin. var(--color-text-muted) measures 4.55:1 on --color-surface-secondary (#f8fafc), which clears the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text.

faq.q: Should I hardcode the muted gray value?
faq.a: No. Reference var(--color-text-muted) after importing @ramoslabs/tokens/css once at the app entry. A raw hex value in CSS is a defect under the design system rules.

sources: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum): 4.5:1 for normal text
